slot.brief: For a hydrogen-like ion or a transition between two given levels, ask the ratio of energies/radii/velocities between two states using Bohr-model formulas.

stem: Using the Bohr model, what is the ratio of the photon energy emitted in the $n=3\to1$ transition of $\text{He}^+$ to that emitted in the $n=2\to1$ transition of $\text{Li}^{2+}$?

verdicts.working: For a hydrogen-like ion, ΔE = 13.6 Z²(1/n_f² − 1/n_i²) eV. The ratio is [4(1 − 1/9)]/[9(1 − 1/4)] = 128/243.

working:
$\Delta E=13.6Z^2\left(\dfrac{1}{n_f^2}-\dfrac{1}{n_i^2}\right)\ \text{eV}$; $\dfrac{\Delta E_{\text{He}^+}}{\Delta E_{\text{Li}^{2+}}}=\dfrac{4(1-1/9)}{9(1-1/4)}=\dfrac{128}{243}$.

Independent check: For a hydrogen-like ion, ΔE = 13.6 Z²(1/n_f² − 1/n_i²) eV. The ratio is [4(1 − 1/9)]/[9(1 − 1/4)] = 128/243.
